newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says to reconsider Eramet situation.
newsitem.headline: France says to reconsider Eramet situation.

text.p: The French government said on Wednesday that it will reconsider the mining situation of Eramet in New Caledonia.
The office of Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said in a statement that the new approach would respect the interests of the company and of its minority shareholders.

It also said France supported a plan to build a new nickel smelter in the north of the island to "rebalance" economic development and had ordered a study on "economic and industrial prospects of such a plant". The study will be conducted before the end of the summer.
The study will be undertaken by Philippe Essig, a former president of state railway operator SNCF, who will also conduct a review of mining assets in the whole of New Caledonia.
The statement added that the state would also insure that New Caledonians will be fairly represented within the company.
In a statement issued after its board meeting, Eramet said it was calling a general shareholders meeting for July 31 and would submit a number of proposals aimed to soothe some minority shareholders.
It said it would propose a new board to the meeting which would include three staff representatives and two "personalities from New Caledonia," who will be named soon.
